summary: Second verification round on revision 2 of the knee-edge OOD draft: three lenses, skeptic re-check, completeness critic

packed.verdict: Revision 2 deals with most of the 23 digest items on paper. The numeric reconciliation is now coherent. The anchors -0.7263/-0.7747, retention 48.2% (42.4/67.6), the L1.4 bands, the removal bounds and the R_deep- counts (19 vs 1,105) all match screens/random_control_mc_output.txt. The slot table checks out in float32. Citations to td3_bc.py, runtime.py and thrusterchain.py check out. The budget arithmetic reproduces. But several resolutions are mis-built in ways that matter. (1) The Stage 2 'native replicate' fix depends on the replicate being independent of the Stage 1 native branch. The prior pipeline derives the branch key from the fork RNG plus a per-seed branch_native_seed (runtime.py:225-228), and r2 never says Stage 2 uses a different seed. So the replicate can be a bit-for-bit rerun. In that case V0-S2 passes automatically, R3's noise-calibrated delta collapses to 2.0, and the regression-to-the-mean rationale is unmet. (2) The text says RANDOM 'copies' control_masks, but that function stratifies on a 2-level load flag, not the 3 bands the sealed values were simulated with. A verbatim copy fails the sealed L1.4 bars about half the time. (3) The new label system still has holes. L1.4 and the 4.7 count bounds carry both INCOMPLETE and INCONCLUSIVE. The INCOMPLETE rerun rule never terminates for failures that recur deterministically. R0's FAIL-early skips validity precedence. Stage 2 reuses 'INCONCLUSIVE' for screens that are only reported. (4) The calibration replacement rule departs from the prior rule it claims to follow, and it oversamples post-stall successor states. A few items are only partly resolved: the corrected step 0.3 forecast is uncomputed and undisclosed, there is no power statement, and the recovery guard has no lower confidence bound. Several terms that r1 defined are now undefined. All of this can be fixed on paper before A1, but the protocol should not be sealed as written.

verified.section: Stage 2 Arms (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:563-565), R3 (:585), V0-S2 (:580); digest item 3/2
verified.claim: The native replicate's seed is never separated from the Stage 1 native branch's. Under the reused pipeline the replicate can be a deterministic rerun of the Stage 1 branch. That would make V0-S2 pass automatically and would collapse R3's delta.
verified.evidence: In the prior pipeline, branch() sets native_key = fold_in(fork rng, seed['branch_native_seed']) and aux_key = fold_in(aux_rng, seed['branch_aux_seed']), with one value per seed index (runtime.py:225-228; protocol.json:354-372). The sampler draws from that key (runtime.py:208-210). R2 says only that 'All three branches from a fork share one pre-registered branch seed and one minibatch stream' (:564). It never says that seed differs from the Stage 1 native branch's. If it is the same, J(rep) - J(Stage 1 native) differs only by GPU nondeterminism. Then delta = max(2.0, 2 x SD) = 2.0, and V0-S2 (K2 and K3a in every seed) repeats the Stage 1 PASS. The selection/regression rationale (:565) is then unaddressed. With delta = 2 and a branch noise SD of about 3.55 (the prior BCA-minus-native SD, :583), R3 passes in all 3 seeds under zero true cost with probability Phi(2/3.55)^3 = 0.36.
verified.fix: In seeds.json, give Stage 2 its own branch_native_seed and branch_aux_seed per fork, distinct from Stage 1's and collision-audited. Assert that the replicate's minibatch-index digest differs from the Stage 1 branch's. State that R3's SD is computed over independent replicates.

check.reason: Revision 2 never separates the Stage 2 replicate's seed from the Stage 1 native branch's seed. In the reused pipeline the branch key does not depend on the arm: branch() uses protocol['seeds'][seed_index]['branch_native_seed'] for native, bca and distance alike. So a replicate forked from the same 10k state is the same run as the Stage 1 native branch, apart from GPU nondeterminism. That undoes the selection fix that V0-S2 and the replicate exist to provide. It also collapses R3's delta to its 2.0 floor, because the SD of J(rep) - J(Stage 1 native) is about 0 when the bank is shared, or only evaluation noise otherwise. Nothing elsewhere in the draft covers this: Part 9 item 21 asks only that the three Stage 2 branches share one seed, which is the shared-random-numbers fix, not independence from Stage 1.
check.evidence: DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:564 says only 'All three branches from a fork share one pre-registered branch seed and one minibatch stream'. No line distinguishes that seed from Stage 1's (grep for seeds/branch seed: lines 418, 488, 564, 725 only). runtime.py:224-226: seed = protocol['seeds'][seed_index]; native_key = fold_in(state.microstep.rng, seed['branch_native_seed']); aux_key = fold_in(state.aux_rng, seed['branch_aux_seed']). The arm is used only for kappa (line 230). The sampler draws from that key (runtime.py:208-210). R3 (:585) uses SD across forks of [J(rep) - J(Stage 1 native)] as 'branch noise'. If the two are identical, delta = 2.0. With a difference SD of 3.55 and zero true cost, P(pass in all 3 seeds) = Phi(0.563)^3 = 0.713^3 = 0.36.

verified.section: Part 3.7 (:226), Part 6.1 (:603), L1.4 known-fault tests (:130), screens/random_control_mc.py:52,68
verified.claim: The text says RANDOM 'copies' the prior control_masks 'exact rule', but that rule stratifies on a 2-level high-load flag. The sealed values assume 3 bands. A verbatim copy is neither accepted nor reliably rejected by L1.4.
verified.evidence: geometry.py:114 builds strata = (episode, time//bin, regions['high']), which has 2 levels. R2 specifies low/mid/deep bands and the MC uses 3 (random_control_mc.py:52). I re-simulated the verbatim 2-band rule (scratchpad verify_wf_r2/resolution/twoband.py, 60 reps). Pooled density is 2.137 (SD 0.017) against the bar [2.00, 2.16], so it fails with P = 0.09. Deep-band density is 2.233 (SD 0.042) against [1.80, 2.24], so it fails with P = 0.43. W retention is 0.490 and the anchor is -0.7761, both inside bounds. The MC's 'band-blind' known fault (sid2 = ep*100 + tb*3 + 0, line 68) has no load term at all, so it is not the 2-band variant. An implementer following 'copies control_masks' therefore gets a coin-flip L1.4 outcome.
verified.fix: State that the rule is control_masks modified to three load bands, and change Part 6.1 to match. Add the verbatim 2-band variant to the MC and seal its expected values. Either make it a known-fault test that must fail (the bars would need tightening), or accept it explicitly.

check.reason: The sentence the finding cites states the three-band stratification explicitly: 'in each stratum (episode x ten-step bin x load band) ... The bands are low (g < 0.4), mid (0.4 <= g < 1.0) and deep (g >= 1.0)' (:226). load_band is defined in 4.1 (:257) and Part 6.1 says 'load band'. 'Copies control_masks' refers to the uniform count-matching mechanics. A literal verbatim copy is not even possible, because the prior third stratum key is regions['high'], an observation-feature region (geometry.py:110), not g >= 0.4. An implementer must use the specified load_band either way. I reproduced the arithmetic (two-band pooled density 2.137 SD 0.017, deep 2.233 SD 0.042, W retention 0.490). L1.4's weak power against a non-compliant two-band variant is a minor coverage nit, not a validity defect: the two variants are scientifically near-equivalent, and the spec rules the two-band one out.
check.evidence: DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:226 defines the three bands in the same sentence as 'copies'. geometry.py:110 builds strata = (episodes, times//time_bin, regions['high']), with regions from region_masks(obs, actions), an observation-based region rather than load g. My re-simulation (scratchpad verify_wf_r2/skeptic_resolution/twoband.py, 60 reps): d3 = 2.083, d2 = 2.137, deep d2 = 2.233, deep d3 = 2.029, wr2 = 0.490.

verified.claim: L1.4 and the 4.7 reconciliation bounds carry two labels. The INCOMPLETE rerun rule has no exit for deterministic failures. Some 'sealed' values cannot be re-derived from the named script.
verified.evidence: 4.7 lists 'L1.4 bands as stated there', RANDOM retention and anchor bounds as count reconciliation. 5.0 and the step 0.4 table map 'count mismatch' to INCOMPLETE, while the same table maps 'L1.4 outside its bands' to INCONCLUSIVE. Precedence makes it INCOMPLETE. The rerun rule repeats the unit 'with identical seeds and streams' (:390). Collection is seeded, so a realized value outside a sealed bound recurs identically, and so does an 'exhausted cap'. No terminal label exists. Separately, 4.7 says its values are 'sealed at A1 from random_control_mc.py', but that script outputs no high-load share, deep share or P(g >= 1.0) (random_control_mc_output.txt). So the bounds [0.53, 0.62], [0.05, 0.11] and 0.078/17.3% fail step 0.2's own rule ('cannot be re-derived from the sealed script: INCOMPLETE').
verified.fix: Split 4.7 into plumbing checks (INCOMPLETE) and expected-value checks (L1.4, retention, anchors: INCONCLUSIVE). After a second identical INCOMPLETE on a deterministic unit or cap, label the step INCONCLUSIVE and stop. Add the shares and the deep-share/P(g >= 1) statistics to random_control_mc.py and derive their bounds there.

check.reason: Two defects are confirmed. (1) 4.7 places expected-value bounds under 'count reconciliation': CUTOFF removed count and fractions, RANDOM W retention, anchors, shares, and 'L1.4 bands as stated there'. The step 0.4 table maps 'count mismatch' to INCOMPLETE, and the only remedy for INCOMPLETE is a rerun 'with identical seeds and streams' (:390). Collection is seeded, so a realized value outside a 6-SD bound recurs exactly, and the protocol has no terminal label or exit. The L1.4 double-listing is a lesser ambiguity, because the step 0.4 table names L1.4 explicitly as INCONCLUSIVE. (2) 4.7 says its values are 'sealed at A1 from random_control_mc.py', but that script outputs no high-load share, no deep share and no P(g >= 1.0). By step 0.2's own rule, those bounds are 'reconciliation value[s] that cannot be re-derived from the sealed script: INCOMPLETE'. The step 0.2 defect is fixable on paper. The deterministic-rerun dead end is a real gap in the label logic.
check.evidence: DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:346-359 (4.7 bounds, including 'L1.4 bands as stated there'). :390 rerun with identical seeds and streams. :396 INCOMPLETE includes 'count mismatch'. :478-479 step 0.4 table. :421 step 0.2 re-derivation rule. screens/random_control_mc_output.txt lists w_ret, dens_*, anchor_*, rdeep_*, removed*, dens_hi_unstrat and dens_hi_bandblind, plus the first-W-step distribution. It has no high-load share, deep share, or P(g >= 1.0)/17.3% statistics, and grep finds no 0.078 or 17.3 in screens/.

verified.claim: FAIL-early is issued at 10k with no validity check and with a mechanistic reading. That contradicts 'first label that applies wins' and 'readings only for FAIL-consistent'.
verified.evidence: R0 checks only the stall CUTOFF R_deep- rate < 0.05 on 32 E2 starts. V0(a), (c), (e) and V1 are all defined at 20k (:515-523), so none is evaluated before R0 stops the run. A collapsed or untrained actor, or a mis-bound dataset, also gives a rate < 0.05. Yet R0 attaches the reading 'the host contained the extrapolation at 10k' (:493), while 5.0 says 'A mechanistic reading is attached only to FAIL-consistent' (:401).
verified.fix: Before R0, require 10k validity: the 4.4 assertions passed, and J_E1 for stall CUTOFF and RANDOM is at least the untrained value + 50 at 10k (a V0(a) analogue). Otherwise label INCONCLUSIVE. Either drop the mechanistic reading or declare FAIL-early, which needs every seed, a FAIL-consistent subtype.

check.reason: R0 issues a terminal FAIL-early at 10k on the stall-CUTOFF R_deep- rate alone, with no validity precondition. The V0 items are all defined at 20k (:515-523). V1/4.4 in-worker assertions would catch a mis-bound dataset as INCOMPLETE, so that part of the finding is covered. A collapsed or undertrained actor is not covered, and it would also give a rate < 0.05. R0 also attaches a mechanistic reading ('the host contained the extrapolation at 10k'), while 5.0 says a reading is attached only to FAIL-consistent. The error is in the conservative direction: it can cause a false stop, never a false PASS. So it matters less than the 20k gates, but the asymmetry with V0(a) and the contradiction with 5.0 are real.
check.evidence: DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:492-494 R0 rule and reading. :398 FAIL-early defined as a FAIL subtype. :401 'A mechanistic reading is attached only to FAIL-consistent'. :515-523 V0(a)-(e), all at 20k. Only V1 (numerical/assertion failures, 5.0 table) applies at 10k.

verified.claim: Stage 2 reuses reserved label words for screens that are only reported. Its NOT-PROMISING subtypes cannot be applied to its pooled criteria, and some screens have no aggregation rule.
verified.evidence: Recovery 'Otherwise ... INCONCLUSIVE' (:589) and the KC repair screen 'otherwise INCONCLUSIVE' (:593) use the same word as the gate label. Under 'INCOMPLETE > INCONCLUSIVE > ... > PROMISING' (:596) with first-applies-wins, a reported-only recovery could override PROMISING. 'NOT-PROMISING (consistent or mixed, as in 5.0)' needs per-seed criteria, but R1's three-seed-mean clause and R3's 12-fork delta are pooled. DETECTION-FAIL ranks below INCONCLUSIVE, yet V0-S2 cannot be evaluated when detection fails, because no branches are trained. Repair screens 2 and 3 give no seed aggregation. D2 (:570) names no world. 5.0's table does not list DETECTION-FAIL, PROMISING or NOT-PROMISING.
verified.fix: Rename the sub-screen outcomes (for example 'not computed (guard)'). Define NOT-PROMISING for pooled clauses. State that DETECTION-FAIL ends Stage 2 before V0-S2 exists. Give every screen an aggregation rule. Name D2's world (stall). Add the Stage 2 labels to 5.0.

check.reason: These are mostly wording and completeness defects in the Stage 2 label logic, and some are substantive. D2 (:570) names no world: D1 says 'in stall CUTOFF', and the 'stall world unless stated' header (:578) comes after the detection block. 'NOT-PROMISING (consistent or mixed, as in 5.0)' is undefined for R1's pooled three-seed-mean clause and for R3's pooled delta. 'Otherwise ... INCONCLUSIVE' inside the reported-only recovery and KC repair screens reuses a reserved label word. Context ('reported only') limits the damage. Not real as claimed: DETECTION-FAIL vs V0-S2. The text says 'Stop ... no BCA branches are trained' (:574), so Stage 2 ends at detection and V0-S2 is never reached, despite the precedence order. Repair screens 2 and 3 are reported only, so their missing aggregation does not affect any label.
check.evidence: DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:569 (D1, stall CUTOFF) vs :570 (D2, no world). :574 DETECTION-FAIL says Stop with no branches trained. :582 R1 pooled mean clause. :585 R3 pooled delta. :589 and :593 use 'INCONCLUSIVE' inside reported-only screens. :596 precedence list.

verified.claim: The calibration replacement rule is not the prior rule it claims to follow, and it systematically oversamples states that come right after a stall.
verified.evidence: The prior calibration_plan keeps the original row if eligible, 'otherwise uniform eligible row in same episode using separate fixed PCG64 seed' (geometry.py:327-346), and fails rather than backfills when an episode has no eligible row. R2 replaces a W row with 'the next row in fixed time order that is not in W'. The W share is 0.575 x 0.494 + 0.425 x 0.2 = 0.369, so about 47 of 128 calibration rows are replacements. Each is the first non-W row after a W run, which is the successor state where the twin worlds first diverge (:218). Calibration therefore over-weights post-stall states in the stall world and differs systematically between worlds. R2 gives no fallback when no later non-W row exists.
verified.fix: Use the prior rule verbatim: the original seeded row, or else a uniform eligible row in the same episode from a separate seed, with no backfill and failing closed. Report the count of replacements.

check.reason: The replacement rule is a new rule, not the prior one. The prior rule takes a uniform eligible row from the same episode with a separate PCG64 seed and fails when an episode has no eligible row. The 'next non-W row' rule also has no fallback when every later row in the episode is in W, and simulation shows that case is likely to occur. It also shifts the replacements toward high load, because g is autocorrelated in time and the neighbor of a W row is usually also high load. The calibration stays common across arms within a world, so the arm comparison is not confounded. The 'differs between worlds' sub-claim is overstated: row indices are world-identical, and states diverge after the first W row under either rule.
check.evidence: DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:234 'If the selected row is in W, the next row in fixed time order that is not in W replaces it'. geometry.py:337-346 prior rule (uniform eligible row in the same episode, separate seed; failed_empty_eligible_episode). Simulation (scratchpad verify_wf_r2/skeptic_resolution/calib.py, 2,000 reps x 128 episodes, stated reset law and recorder): 47.4 replacements per world, 0.877 expected episodes with no later non-W row, P(at least one) = 0.59. The high-load share of replacements is 0.714 under the next-row rule vs 0.596 under the prior uniform-eligible rule.

packed.verdict: Revision 2 fixes the structure of the rule system. FAIL-consistent and FAIL-mixed are now mutually exclusive. G0.5 is relabelled INCONCLUSIVE. K3c is the same-policy world swap, V0(b) is two-sided, and the ratio screens are guarded. Several of the new rules, though, still do not measure what they claim, or are too noisy to decide anything. (1) Digest item 1 is not actually resolved. Fitting the step 0.3 quadratic only on {-0.5,-0.6,-0.7,-KNEE} still measures the old critics' labelled fold, because a critic that rounds the slope-1.5 kink bends Q1 at -0.7 and -KNEE. With a rounding width of only 0.02 in a0, the forecast moves from -0.95 to -0.85 (not in R_deep-) while G0.5's F stays at 0.000. The 4-point design also multiplies critic noise by 25x in the extrapolated slope, so the forecast drifts toward about 50% whatever the true slopes are. (2) Stage 2 R1 is weak. Using the saved same-fork BCA-minus-native spreads, which share CRN exactly as Stage 2 will, its false-positive rate under the null is about 9-10%, and its power against a true +3 gain is only about 33%. The prior study's own hole-vs-random cells at strong current, 15k, pass both R1 (+2.68/+1.61/+10.17) and R2, although that study found nothing hole-specific. Episode-level SEs are 0.3-0.6, so the noise is branch-training noise, and a larger bank cannot fix it. critic.verdict: Revision 2 is NOT ready to seal at A1. Two high-severity defects remain, and both change gate logic. (1) Nothing separates the Stage 2 native replicate's seed from the Stage 1 native branch's seed. The reused pipeline derives the branch key from the fork RNG and a per-seed-index branch_native_seed (runtime.py:224-228), and the arm does not enter that key. So the replicate can be a bit-for-bit rerun of the selected Stage 1 branch. V0-S2 would then pass automatically, R3's delta would collapse to its 2.0 floor, and the regression-to-the-mean fix would be lost. (2) The step 0.3 reach gating fit is a four-point quadratic on {-0.5,-0.6,-0.7,-KNEE}. The -KNEE point sits on the old critics' labelled fold. Rounding that kink over 0.02 moves the forecast from -0.95 to -0.85, out of R_deep-, while G0.5 stays clean (F(-1)=0.000). The design also amplifies noise to sd(c)=50 sigma. Seven medium items remain: R1 has roughly 5-10% null pass and about 0.3 power, with neither disclosed. R3 has no difference-in-differences, so a generic BCA gain masks a knee-specific cost. The V0(b) bar of 0.25 is near what a smooth but correctly labelled RANDOM critic produces. The 4.7 expected-value bounds are routed to INCOMPLETE with a deterministic rerun and no exit, and the share bars are not derivable from the sealed script. The calibration replacement rule is new and undefined in a case with P about 0.57. Arithmetic, citations, slot table, L1.4 bands, anchors, budget and hashes all check out. Refuted, or downgraded to wording only: the 'copies control_masks' validity claim (the text states three bands) and the step 0.3 forecast-disclosure item (step 0.3 is itself the gate, and its error runs in the conservative direction). I made three spot-checks no lens covered. (a) Part 3.10 says E1 is 'reported only' (DRAFT_PROTOCOL.md:239), yet V0(a) gates on J_E1 (:519). V0(a) also checks RANDOM's learning only: CUTOFF has no adequacy check, so a CUTOFF actor that does not learn but passes the binding assertions gives a K2 FAIL-consistent with the wrong reading 'the BC anchor contains the over-valuation'. The +50 bar is lenient: in the prior study, untrained to native-20k ordinary discounted J rose from -237/-261/-313 to about -76 to -81, a gain of 155-235. (b) R0's 32 E2 starts have no named stream, and the text does not say how they relate to the 128-start gated bank (:492 vs :496-497). (c) thrust() applies the knee elementwise to all four thrusters (thrusterchain.py:190-198). The design's a1..a3 bound of 0.7 together with V0(e) and Part 6.10 handles this consistently, so it is checked OK.

must_fix.issue: Nothing requires the replicate's branch seed to differ from the Stage 1 native branch seed. In runtime.py:224-228, native_key = fold_in(fork rng, seed['branch_native_seed']), one per seed index and independent of the arm. A replicate forked from the same 10k state is then the Stage 1 branch again, apart from GPU nondeterminism. Consequences: V0-S2 repeats the Stage 1 PASS, SD of [J(rep) - J(Stage 1 native)] is about 0 so delta = 2.0, and with a true branch-noise SD of about 3.55 R3 passes in all 3 seeds under zero cost with P = Phi(2/3.55)^3 = 0.36. R3 also names no bank: the Stage 1 native branch was evaluated on the Stage 1 bank and the replicate on a new Stage 2 bank (:566), and the SD's pooling across 12 heterogeneous forks and its ddof are unspecified.

Assert that the replicate's minibatch-index digest differs from the Stage 1 branch's. Re-evaluate the Stage 1 native branch on the Stage 2 bank before computing delta, or seal delta as a number now (see R3 item). Compute any SD from the 9 forks not selected for damage, or within each arm-world cell, with ddof stated.

must_fix.issue: The four-point quadratic on {-0.5,-0.6,-0.7,-KNEE} still carries the old critics' labelled fold, because -KNEE is the kink. Softplus rounding of width 0.02 gives c=-3.47 and pi0=-0.850, which is not in R_deep-, while F(-1)=0.000. Width 0.05 gives pi0=-0.785. The design is also ill-conditioned: sd(c)=50 sigma and sd(Q'(-0.9))=25.4 sigma, against 5.5 sigma for six points. At sigma=0.05, a row whose true pi0 is -0.95 counts as reaching only 76% of the time, and a row at -0.85 counts 24% of the time, so the forecast is pulled toward 50%. The error runs toward a false FAIL(reach) that records 'old critics forecast no reach'. Line 458's defence covers false positives only.

residual_risks: Even after the fixes, Stage 2's PROMISING label is a weak screen. With 3 seeds and branch-training noise of about 3.5 return units, a method with no real knee-specific benefit passes R1 roughly 5-10% of the time, and a real +3 benefit is detected only about a third of the time. Treat PROMISING as 'worth a bigger study', not as evidence that BCA works.
Stage 1 has no power estimate. Six criteria and five validity items must hold in every one of three seeds, so a true effect can still come out FAIL-mixed. A FAIL-mixed says nothing either way.

Reach is the main feasibility risk. The old critics' slopes near the knee are extrapolated and the margins are thin, so step 0.3 or R0 may stop the plan early. Those stops cost little compute but end the line of work. A false stop is more likely than a false pass.

The validity bar on RANDOM's knee representation (V0(b)) may trip for a correctly labelled but smooth critic, which would make Stage 1 INCONCLUSIVE regardless of the hypothesis unless the bar is rescaled.

Several sealed expected values (count bounds, shares, L1.4 bands) are deterministic given the seeds. If the realized data fall outside a bound, the current rules have no way to finish. That needs the INCOMPLETE/INCONCLUSIVE split before sealing.

Every claim is confined to Unifloral TD3+BC on the stall_slope 3.0 world of knee_edge_v1, with a1..a3 bounded to 0.7. Thruster commands in (0.7, 0.8] are unlogged in every arm, so a shared extrapolation region exists that the knee condition does not control.

The prior study's own data show how fragile checkpoint-level contrasts are. The hole-vs-random gain flipped from +2.68/+1.61/+10.17 at 15k to -1.02/+6.22/-1.94 at 20k. Gating on 20k alone is correct, but expect sign instability across seeds.
